news.title: CYMRU WOMEN: World Cup play-off decider against Albania comes to Parc y Scarlets on Tuesday
news.lede: Cymru Women’s World Cup hopes come to Llanelli on Tuesday, when they play the second leg of their play-off against Albania at Parc y Scarlets. Kick-off is at 7.15pm on Tuesday 13 October. The first leg is tonight at the Loro Boriçi Stadium in Shkodër, Albania, with kick-off at 5pm UK time. The tie is decided on aggregate over the two legs.

news.title: African football chiefs back Infantino to remain as Fifa boss
news.lede: Gianni Infantino's bid to remain the head of world football's governing body Fifa gathered strength on Friday after backing from African executives and reports that a potential rival was pulling out of the race for the job as the game's most powerful administrator. Issued on: 09/10/2026 - 15:14Modified: 09/10/2026 - 15:15. The president of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), Patrice Motsepe, hailed Infantino on Thursday for his support for African football during a three-day CAF strategy meeting on Sal island in Cape Verde. "We took a resolution, unanimous that we support him and we will stand by him for the next elections," Motsepe said in an address to delegates from the 54 national federations that form the CAF.

news.title: CAF boss Motsepe backs African nation to win FIFA World Cup
news.lede: Patrice Motsepe, president of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), has expressed confidence that an African nation will eventually win the FIFA World Cup, challenging the continent to turn its growing competitiveness into football’s biggest prize. Speaking at the CAF Strategy Conference in Santa Maria, on Sal Island in Cape Verde, Motsepe said African teams had shown the ability to compete against the world’s strongest football nations and must now aspire to win the global title. “We know how good we are, and the world has seen how good we are,” Motsepe said. “We have to win the World Cup one day.

news.title: FIFA Reportedly Allowed Ineligible DR Congo Player In 2026 World Cup
news.lede: FIFA, the world football governing body, allowed the Democratic Republic of Congo to compete in this year’s World Cup hosted by Canada, the USA and Mexico, despite reports that an internal investigation found the country fielded an ineligible player in qualifying. The player in question, goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, starred for DR Congo at the tournament, including against England in the last 32. Mpasi, who was born in France and played for Les Bleus at youth level, had never completed the process of switching nationalities, FIFA reportedly found. No punishment was levied against the Congolese federation, FECOFA.

news.title: The Fifth Ulcinj World Cup: Tribute to Gudelj, Vujošević, Dalipagić, Koprivica...
news.lede: Another gathering of sports greats from the former state will have an emotional opening tonight at 19 pm at the Ulcinj Cultural Center. The fifth Ulcinj Friendship World Cup - an event that has already become recognizable in almost every corner of the entire region - will begin tonight in the southernmost Montenegrin city. It will start symbolically: with some kind of tribute, a remembrance for the five greats and heroes of the Friendship World Cup who have passed away in the meantime. These include the celebrated Hajduk captain and Yugoslav national team player Ivan Gudelj, then the writer Božo Koprivica, water polo player Goran Sukno, basketball coaching icon Duško Vujošević and the absolute legend of the game under the hoops, Dražen Praja Dalipagić.
